chapter: Family background and the Tulsa music scene
title: Segregated dances for Duke and Cab
summary: Big bands played Black dances at separate Tulsa halls.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When a band would come to town, a traveling band, and play, say, Thursday nights in the Negro section, would that band maybe play Saturday night in the white section for a white audience?

Sometimes. There was a dance hall there called the Skyline. That was a public dance. Now, when Duke and Cab came to town, Duke would generally play the convention hall, and Cab would be at some arena where they held hockey games, you know. It was an arena, like.
Did everybody go, or was it restricted?
No, this was black dances, you know.
Was there ever anything that both blacks and whites could go to?
